riso.wins: The fastest hero to find of all six, and the only board where counting a sprat's length stays effortless — flat inks, hard edges, no soft falloff. The most distinctive thing here; it looks like a printed poster rather than a game asset.
riso.costs: The door is framed in her exact fluorescent pink, so at the one moment the game most wants you to watch her — swimming out — she and the opening share an ink. Not in the game — kept here as a drawn alternative.

deco.wins: The best-made object in the review. The lid wound onto a real winding key is the most convincing opened tin anyone drew, and the whole thing could be the game's identity rather than a skin.
deco.costs: The hole itself is a thin dark slot that's easy to miss on a phone, and the gilded hero reads expensive rather than magical — her eye is a cut gem, so she's the one sprat with no pupil.

neon.wins: You can see the way out from across the room, and the hero actually emits light — the fastest find of the six by a distance, and the most dramatic board.
neon.costs: It trades the warm oily tin for a dark aquarium, and a glow is the first thing a compressed screenshot throws away — which is how this game spreads.

holo.wins: The everyday sprats are the best-looking fish here, and the most truthful — a real Baltic sprat is exactly this oil-slick chrome.
holo.costs: The hero is pale against warm oil, so she takes about a second to find; she's the one fish in the set that looks less crafted than her own extras. Not in the game — kept here as a drawn alternative.

paper.wins: A white cut-edge around every fish makes length and lane effortless to read — the calmest, most legible board of the six, and the hero has the best face.
paper.costs: She's carried by saturation, and saturation is the first thing to die in sunlight; her silhouette then has to find her on its own. Not in the game — kept here as a drawn alternative.

plush.wins: The most literal answer to unicorny — spiral horn, rainbow felt mane, heart tail, stitched seams. The funniest object anyone drew, and the one board that looks like a toy you would want.
plush.costs: The warm bellies sit close to the oil, so at phone size the sprats sink into the board — the least legible of the six, and the hero is found by her colour rather than her shape.

classic.wins: Warm, legible, and the look the game has always had — it stays the default, so nobody arriving from a link meets a stranger.
classic.costs: It is the plainest of the four, and the little one is still a pink version of the same fish rather than a creature of her own.
